claims: Session-only project trust decisions grant access for the current process without persisting consent.
Project trust resolution runs exactly once per bootstrap pass and receives the extension set loaded while the project was still untrusted.
Changing project trust actually switches SettingsManager state and reloads project settings.
An extension project_trust decision is persisted only when remember === true, for approvals and denials alike.
Trust resolution never mutates global configuration; only ~/.pi/agent/trust.json can be written, and only on explicit remember: true.

validation.notes: Cross-module regression links the real settings-manager, resource-loader, project-trust, and trust-manager modules through .prale-eval/subject.mjs; only process boundaries are faked (temp project/agent dirs, chalk, proper-lockfile, package/extension discovery, project_trust event emitter). Checks: (1) SettingsManager.setProjectTrusted toggles trust false->true->false, loads project settings on grant and drops them on denial, and never rewrites global settings.json; (2) DefaultResourceLoader.reload({resolveProjectTrust}) keeps the bootstrap untrusted (resolver observes isProjectTrusted()===false and only user extensions), calls the resolver exactly once, applies its decision to settings, loads project settings/extensions on approval and omits them on denial, and does not re-resolve on a plain reload; (3) resolveProjectTrusted persists only for remember===true (approval and denial), keeps {trusted:'yes'} / remember:false / session-only prompt choices ephemeral, reuses saved decisions, honours --approve/--no-approve overrides, and leaves global settings untouched. Detection verified by restoring each file alone to its faulty baseline: settings-manager.ts ('setProjectTrusted(true) must update the trust state'), resource-loader.ts ('the trust resolver must run exactly once per reload'), project-trust.ts (session-only persistence assertion) each fail with an assertion, not a crash or import error. Temp fixtures live under .prale-eval/tmp and are removed after the run. Limitation: no installed dependencies in this workspace, so vitest/tsc/biome cannot be executed; the regression script is the focused validation.
